question:
A 62-year-old woman seeks a second medical opinion following the insertion of an intramedullary nail
through what was initially thought to be a metastatic lesion in her proximal femur. Subsequent biopsy
results reveal a high-grade chondrosarcoma, and staging studies indicate this is an isolated lesion.
What is the most appropriate treatment recommendation? Answer Choices: (A) Systemic
chemotherapy and keep nail in place to prevent fracture (B) Observation and serial imaging after nail
removal (C) Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by limb salvage surgery (D) External beam radiation
with concurrent chemotherapy (E) Wide resection including hip disarticulation (F) Limb-sparing surgery
with endoprosthetic reconstruction (G) Targeted radiation therapy with nail removal (H) Wide excision
with total femoral replacement (I) Curettage and bone grafting with prophylactic fixation (J) Wide
proximal femoral resection and hemiarthroplasty followed by radiotherapy
 A. Wide excision with total femoral replacement
B. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by limb salvage surgery
C. Wide proximal femoral resection and hemiarthroplasty followed by radiotherapy
D. Curettage and bone grafting with prophylactic fixation
E. Targeted radiation therapy with nail removal
F. Systemic chemotherapy and keep nail in place to prevent fracture
G. Observation and serial imaging after nail removal
H. Limb-sparing surgery with endoprosthetic reconstruction
I. Wide resection including hip disarticulation
J. External beam radiation with concurrent chemotherapy
